core.title: Author every file beneath the documentation root in the stack's documentation markup format, never in the rejected alternate format
core.given: A plan artifact, product slice or documentation change places an authored file beneath the documentation root (any path not beneath the generated documentation-output tree).
core.when: The planner chooses the file's format or path.
core.then: An authored file beneath the documentation root (outside the generated documentation-output tree) MUST use the stack's documentation markup format; a file of the rejected alternate format there is a violation.
prefer: Convert an existing file of the rejected format beneath the documentation root to the same path in the documentation markup format, keeping its content intact.
When converting a historical document, place it in the documentation tree's archive area and set its status marker accordingly; migration preserves history and never promotes it to current.
Decide by location only: beneath the documentation root, not beneath the generated documentation-output tree, in the rejected format - convert.
avoid: Committing an authored file of the rejected format anywhere beneath the documentation root outside the generated documentation-output tree.
Arguing a file of the rejected format beneath the documentation root is exempt because it is 'not really prose documentation' - the test is location, not content.
Treating format conversion as making a historical document current.

Expanding the plan to reject or convert files of the rejected format outside the documentation tree (repository readme, contribution guide, repository-root corpus) under this rule; that migration belongs to the adoption step.
unless: The file is beneath the generated documentation-output tree (generated build output, never scanned).
The file of the rejected format is outside the documentation tree (e.g. the repository readme or contribution guide); it is migrated by the adoption step, not rejected here.
core.why: A corpus in two markup formats cannot serve as one documentation tree: the other documentation rules attach document identifiers and implements/supersedes-style relationship edges only under a single uniform format, so format uniformity is the precondition for every other documentation rule.
evidence: A scan of the documentation tree (excluding the generated documentation-output tree by path) reports zero files of the rejected alternate format.
Converted files exist at the same path in the documentation markup format with preserved content; historical ones sit in the archive area with their status marker set.
verification: Deterministic location test, not a content test: flag a file iff it is beneath the documentation root, not beneath the generated documentation-output tree, and carries the rejected alternate format's suffix. 'Is this really prose documentation?' is semantic and undecidable, so the decidable location form is chosen on purpose.

Authored means: anything beneath the documentation root that is not beneath the generated documentation-output tree is authored. The generated output tree is produced by the documentation build, normally ignored by version control, and never subject to the authored-format rule.

Exclude the generated documentation-output tree by path rather than by version-control ignore status, so the check is identical whether or not the tree has been built - deterministic in continuous integration.
Files of the rejected format outside the documentation tree are out of scope for this check; their migration belongs to the adoption step of the stack's documentation model.
Disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline. Severity 2.

fires: A plan artifact or product slice creates a new file of the rejected alternate format beneath the documentation root.
An existing file of the rejected format is moved or copied into the documentation tree (outside the generated documentation-output tree).
A scan of the documentation tree finds any committed file of the rejected format not beneath the generated documentation-output tree.
doesNotFire: A file of the rejected format beneath the generated documentation-output tree (generated build output, never scanned).
Files of the rejected format outside the documentation tree, including the repository readme, contribution guide and repository-root corpus.
A file in the stack's documentation markup format authored anywhere beneath the documentation root.

profileRequirements.meaning: Root of the authored documentation tree; the rule's location test and every scoping statement (given, unless, activation binding, check scope) are relative to this root.

The stack's generated output trees (documentation, renders, views) that are outputs, never authored inputs; this rule takes the generated documentation-output tree beneath the documentation root as its never-scanned exception.
Suffixes of the stack's documentation markup format - the one authored format permitted beneath the documentation root.

Suffixes of the alternate prose-markup format rejected beneath the documentation root; the check flags exactly this suffix (not every non-markup suffix), and the activation kind rejected_markup_beneath_documentation_root binds it to the documentation root.
Directory beneath the documentation root where historical documents are placed when converted; conversion puts them there and never promotes them to current.
How a document declares its status (current vs historical/archived) in the stack's documentation markup format; a converted historical document sets it accordingly.

bunOnly.text: doc-id and :implements:/:supersedes: edges are AsciiDoc attributes and markdown has nowhere to put them
bunOnly.reason: The concrete representational mechanism (AsciiDoc attributes vs markdown's lack of them) is specific to the ATDD-Bun documentation model's format pair; the core states only the general uniform-format rationale - the relationship graph presupposes one format - and makes no claim about other stacks' format capacities.

bunOnly.text: (spec 2 §4 chose the decidable form on purpose; same reasoning as planner.docs.undeclared-change being the enforceable inverse of 'should this have been declared?')
bunOnly.reason: Cites the ATDD-Bun handoff spec and a sibling Bun rule id; lineage reasoning, not part of the neutral obligation. The decidable-location-test rationale itself is kept in core verification.

bunOnly.text: rendered by the build (spec 2 §7), normally excluded from git
bunOnly.reason: Cites the ATDD-Bun handoff spec and git by name; the core says 'produced by the documentation build, normally ignored by version control'.

bunOnly.text: Fix-hint example: docs/architecture/shared-control-root.md (✗ authored markdown under docs/) → docs/architecture/shared-control-root.adoc (✓ authored AsciiDoc)
bunOnly.reason: Rule-specific example paths and the concrete format pair; bun.json itself is delivered as the worked reference example, so the core does not repeat it.

Term generated_output neutralized; the tree's identity comes from the stack's generated output trees (roots.generated), selected beneath the documentation root; the spec 2 §7 / git wording is bunOnly.

Exclusion of the generated documentation-output tree by path rather than by ignore status, so the check is identical whether or not the tree has been built; bun.json requires nothing more, and the core adds nothing more.

path_glob 'docs/**/*.md' re-typed as a scoped file_kind fact: rejected_markup_beneath_documentation_root binds the rejected suffix (suffix.rejected_markup) to the documentation root (roots.docs), so the fact fires only beneath that root - exactly Bun's docs/**/*.md.

path_glob '!docs/dist/**' re-typed as a negative file_kind fact: !generated_output_beneath_documentation_root excludes, by path, the generated documentation-output tree beneath the documentation root (roots.generated beneath roots.docs); the '!' preserves Bun's exclusion polarity, so files there never fire.
Change kinds are already neutral; tree-scan semantics kept.
Task terms are stack-neutral planner vocabulary; kept verbatim.

neutralityNotes: The required and rejected formats (.adoc / .md), the documentation root (docs), the generated documentation-output tree (docs/dist/**), the archive area (docs/archive/) and the status marker (:status:) are profile data, bound through existing vocabulary v3 keys: roots.docs, roots.generated, suffix.markup, suffix.rejected_markup, layout.locations#docs_archive and idiom.docs_syntax#doc_status_marker - no keys are proposed. The generated-output exception is the generated documentation-output tree beneath the documentation root, taken from the stack's generated output trees (roots.generated, which covers generated documentation output) rather than the stack-wide roots.excluded union; it is excluded by path rather than by version-control ignore status, so the check is identical whether or not the tree has been built - bun.json imposes no further exclusion architecture, and the core adds none. The Bun path_glob activation facts were re-typed as scoped file_kind facts - rejected_markup_beneath_documentation_root binds the rejected suffix to the documentation root, and !generated_output_beneath_documentation_root keeps the exclusion's negative polarity - so the fact mapping alone admits exactly the files Bun's facts admit (beneath the root, rejected suffix, outside the generated tree); prose exceptions add no further scope. The core's why states only the general uniform-format rationale; the claim that the rejected format has nowhere to carry relationship attributes is the ATDD-Bun format-pair mechanism and stays in bunOnly. Per-rule severity 2 and the strict disposition (including the sharedNodes policy.strict-disposition node) are carried in core verification, not the profile. The audit, trace, additions and sharedNodes blocks and the validator id (docs_capability) are realization bookkeeping outside the agent-facing item numbering. Instantiating the core with the Bun profile values (docs; docs/dist/**; .adoc; .md; docs/archive/; :status:) plus the bunOnly items reproduces bun.json's obligation exactly: flag iff beneath docs/, not beneath docs/dist/, ending .md; convert to the same path in .adoc with content preserved, historical ones into docs/archive/ with :status: set; no exception dropped, no new obligation added.
